## POST `/api/2.58/data-sealing-keys`

**Tier:** T1+ (check: some POSTs are actions)  

The creation of `data sealing keys` for `data-isolated realms`. The `key` can be stored on an external `key management server` (e.g., `KMIP`), or provided as `keying material`. The `names` parameter is required and must specify the fully qualified name in the format `realm_name::data_sealing_key`.

## PATCH `/api/2.58/data-sealing-keys`

**Tier:** T2 (T3 if it destroys, eradicates, disables or overwrites)

## POST `/api/2.58/data-sealing-keys/revoke`

**Tier:** T1+ (check: some POSTs are actions)  

Revokes data sealing keys, performing a cryptographic purge of all data protected by the key. This is an irreversible operation. After revocation, `key_status` is set to `revoked` and the realm's `data_availability_status` is set to `crypto-purged`. The `permanently_erase_data` query parameter must be set to `true` and the `realms` array must be provided in the request body as explicit confirmation of the affected realms. For `local-in-memory` keys, the current `keying_material` must also be provided. Manual eradication must be enabled on the realm and all protection groups and pods within…

## POST `/api/2.58/data-sealing-keys/rotate`

**Tier:** T1+ (check: some POSTs are actions)  

The rotation of the keying material for `data sealing keys`. For `remote keys`, the `key` is automatically rotated on the external `key management server` and no `request body` is required. For `local-in-memory keys`, both the `new keying material` and the `old keying material` must be provided in the `request body`. The `names` parameter is required and must specify the fully qualified name in the format `realm_name::data_sealing_key`.
